subject.title: fix(sandbox): bound SSH command output buffering at 16 MiB

question: Should SSH sandbox commands retain the shared 100 MiB per-stream sandbox limit, adopt a distinct 16 MiB per-stream limit, or enforce a true 16 MiB combined stdout-plus-stderr budget?
rationale: All three choices bound memory, but they differ in compatibility, maximum gateway allocation, and whether sandbox backends share one command-output contract; code inspection cannot determine the intended product policy.

options.title: Keep the shared limit
options.body: Retain the current shared 100 MiB cap and close this PR because current main already fixes the unbounded-buffer problem without adding an SSH-specific policy source.

options.title: Adopt 16 MiB per stream
options.body: Accept the narrower SSH-specific compatibility break, but update the public explanation and proof to state clearly that stdout and stderr each receive a 16 MiB allowance.

options.title: Enforce 16 MiB combined
options.body: Replace the per-stream maxBuffer approach with a shared combined-byte budget and add simultaneous stdout/stderr coverage before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep the shared limit
recommendation.body: Retain the current shared 100 MiB cap and close this PR because current main already fixes the unbounded-buffer problem without adding an SSH-specific policy source.

likelyOwner.reason: The core SSH backend and its contract originated in their commit, and they are also connected to the recent merged output-handling work.
